It sounds really exhausting to feel that scattered and frustrated all day—that's a hard thing to carry, and it makes sense you want answers.

To be honest, no one can diagnose ADHD from a description alone, and it's not something you can figure out just by asking whether you're "normal." Lots of people have busy minds sometimes, but if racing thoughts and trouble focusing are affecting you this much, that's worth taking seriously regardless of the label. Your teacher noticing something is a real signal, and your dad may just want to reassure you rather than dismiss you.

The clearest path is an evaluation by a doctor, psychologist, or your school counselor, who can actually assess what's going on. It might help to write down specific examples of what you struggle with to share with them. Wanting to understand your own brain isn't overreacting—it's a smart step toward feeling more in control.
